summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR 932 crores and FY26 PAT rose 113% to INR 139 crores, with copper cathode capex of about INR 200 crores funded from internal accruals.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 production, sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with FY26 revenue of INR 2,939 crores (+45%) and EBITDA of INR 218 crores (7.4% margin). Q4 EBITDA was INR 61 crores and PAT INR 38 crores, with Q4 blended gross margin of 6.4% pulled down by a copper mix of about 40% and copper margins of about 3.5-4%. Operating cash flow was negative in FY26, which management attributed to about INR 265 crores of trade receivables, mainly an export shipment delayed by vessel movement that pushed INR 120-130 crores of collections into early April. Management also disclosed a 36,000 tpa copper cathode plant (Phase 1 of 18,000 tpa targeted for December 2026) and some trading volumes in Q4, which it said were opportunistic.

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled YoY; margin 7.4% vs 5.3% in FY25 (+212 bps)
Q4 consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT +78% / +124% / +126% YoY
Lead ~45 days; copper brought from ~70 days to around 50 days

financial_highlights.value: INR 5 per share (100% of face value)

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: FY26 production 104,481 MT and sales 100,727 MT (+11% each); value-added products were 65% of lead revenue. Q4 lead volumes dipped as management deliberately prioritised higher-margin products; EBITDA per ton was INR 19,739 in Q4.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Recycling capacity doubled to 12,000 MTPA in Q4 FY26, with ramp to 70% utilisation during FY27. FY26 copper volumes rose about 7x and sales about 11x to INR 673 crores, with EBITDA per ton of INR 39,896. Copper contributed about 40% of Q4 sales at a margin of about 3.5-4%.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Unit relocated and production started in March 2026 at the new location. Management said it is EBITDA and PAT positive as of now, but FY26 was largely negative; per-ton realisation not disclosed.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Little activity; management said it will look at it when the time is right.

guidance_outlook: FY27 lead volume guidance of about 125,000-130,000 MT (management said 70-75% utilisation of the 204,000 MTPA TKD lead capacity), with about 15% lead volume growth targeted for FY28; FY28 utilisation aspiration 80-90%.
FY27 copper volume of about 12,000 MT including cathode; FY28 copper volume of at least 24,000 MT on a conservative basis, with up to about 36,000 MT by end FY28 mentioned.
EBITDA per ton guidance: lead INR 17,000-19,000; copper recycling INR 35,000-40,000; copper cathode INR 60,000-70,000 (conservative), with blended FY28 copper around INR 60,000 cited as achievable.

Phase 1 of 36,000 MTPA copper cathode plant (18,000 MTPA each in two phases) targeted for December 2026, with Phase 2 about 6-7 months later; estimated investment about INR 200 crores funded through internal accruals.
Capex of INR 180-200 crores in FY27 and about INR 50-60 crores in FY28; management said no term loan planned and no new debt contemplated.

Long-term targets: 20% volume growth, 20% revenue and profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 8%, ROCE above 20%, value-added products above 60% of revenue. Other expenses guided at INR 20-25 crores per quarter going forward. Inventory days targeted below 45.
capex_capacity: TKD lead recycling capacity raised 55% to 204,000 MTPA (from 132,000); operated at about 65% in FY26, with ramp to about 75% targeted in coming quarters.
Copper recycling capacity doubled to 12,000 MTPA in Q4 FY26; over 3,000 MT produced in Q4 per analyst question; ramp to 70% during FY27.
Copper cathode plant: 36,000 MTPA at TKD, Tamil Nadu, using integrated pyrorefining and electrorefining to make LME grade A cathodes; Phase 1 of 18,000 MTPA by December 2026.
Mundra project expected to start up in FY27 (no detail given).
FY26 capex of about INR 49 crores; FY27 INR 180-200 crores; FY28 INR 50-60 crores.
demand_pricing: Imports made up about 73% of lead procurement, 61% of plastic and 98% of copper in FY26.

Lead premium: management did not give a per-ton premium figure, attributing high realisations to niche alloys where POCL is a single-point source for certain customers; an analyst's estimate of about $700/t was not confirmed.

Copper sourcing: shipping lead times up 10-15 days due to Middle East conflict; contracts are CIF, so payments are not affected, and procurement is being diversified to Southeast Asia and domestic sources. Outbound freight impact about $2/t.
Copper scrap formula: management said margins are protected through hedging of metal and FX, and that purchase and sale formulas move together.
Industry outlook: management expects copper consumption to rise from about 1.2 million tons to 3-3.5 million tons over 3-4 years, citing energy transition and infrastructure demand.
Trading: Q4 included opportunistic copper trading (about INR 122 crores of purchases of stock in trade), which management said is not the core focus and is not expected to be a regular feature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory/goods rise in Q4 and is it repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 included a copper trading opportunity with better margins than usual; it cannot say it will recur, though some trading has always occurred. Focus remains on manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite strong profits, and what is the receivables split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the trade receivables of about INR 265 crores were a point-in-time effect from an export consignment delayed by vessel movement, with INR 120-130 crores received around April 5. Vijay Balakrishnan said receivables are all finished goods; inventory rose only about INR 36 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 180 crore capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be funded through internal accruals with no term loan. Total reserves plus equity is about INR 800 crores, borrowings about INR 150 crores (all short-term), and there is no long-term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mark-to-market charge of about INR 7 crores in the prior quarter reversed in Q4, and efficiencies across power, fuel and environmental costs lowered costs. Other expenses are expected at INR 20-25 crores per quarter going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper EBITDA per ton after cathode integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cathode is targeted at INR 60,000-70,000 per ton versus INR 35,000-40,000 for current recycling, on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Lead volume outlook versus the 204,000 MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 lead volume target is about 125,000-130,000 MT, with the 70% utilisation referring to the new TKD plant; some lines are capacity-limited by product mix. New products and customers were added.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 blended margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lead margins remained above 8%, while copper (about 40% of sales) runs at about 3.5-4%, bringing the blended margin to 6.4% in Q4.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 operating cash flow driven by INR 265 crore receivables; watch Q1 FY27 collections and whether cash flow turns positive.
Q4 lead volume dip (deliberate mix shift) versus FY27 guidance of 125,000-130,000 MT; the delivery of volume growth depends on the new TKD lines ramping up.
Copper cathode commissioning (Phase 1 by December 2026) and the INR 60,000-70,000/t margin target are not yet supported by trial production data.
Middle East conflict causing 10-20 day shipment delays and rising logistics costs; management says CIF contracts limit payment impact.
Copper price and FX volatility; management says it hedges fully, but Q4 margins were squeezed by copper mix.
Plastics unit recently moved; PAT positive status is early and per-ton figures have not been disclosed.
Lithium-ion recycling: management is studying feedstock and chemistry, with battery stock expected around 2028, but no capex is committed.
key_quotes: FY26 stands as one of the most remarkable years in POCL's journey with the company delivering all -time high production and sales volumes, revenue, EBITDA, PAT and profitability margins.
And I cannot specifically say that it will continue, but definitely, there will be some trading, which has always been there.
This is only a short-term blip. It's not a big blip. It was a conscious decision.
So technically around April 5, we received close to about INR 120 crores to INR 130 crores in payment in that immediate next week.
Q1 is a forward-looking statement. There is always growth is there in the current quarter. That's what we can say. Beyond that, it's not correct on our part to reveal the numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 results, growth targets and debt-free balance sheet, but cautious and deflecting on Q1 FY27 utilisation, copper cathode margins before trial production, and the trading-driven Q4 gross margin. Management repeatedly declined to quantify premiums, peer comparisons, or Q1 numbers, and framed the INR 265 crore receivables as a point-in-time timing issue.
